scope: Read-only source audit, not measured attribution of native retention
findings: Native ArosPlatformTask TaskEntry executes CRT leave hooks but has no pthread TLS destructor loop. The registered posixc leave hook only closes its per-task library base.
SDK pthread foreign task slots are task-local but documented to never run destructors. Chromium base TLS and PartitionAlloc cache TLS currently use those keys.
PartitionAlloc cache Delete destructor unregisters the thread cache and purges cached allocations; absent exit callback is a supported retention hypothesis.
Compiler emutls AROS backend allocates arrays/values without a cleanup path; freeing these before CRT or C++ destructors finish would be unsafe.
Task resource slot storage does not imply destruction of pointed-to allocations.
next: Measure active/dead task cache counts and bytes, then implement Chromium-owned native task exit lifecycle; cover native worker and DOS main task, destructor reentrancy, ordering, no cached data use after free. No SDK mmap or global pthread changes.
